results.text: 736.0802 General standards of trustee's duties.—(1) A trustee shall administer the trust in good faith, according to its terms and purpose and the purposes of the trust and in accordance with this chapter and the Prudent Investor Act, chapter 718.

736.0803 Impartiality.—If a trust has 2 or more beneficiaries, the trustee shall act impartially in investing, managing, and distributing trust property, unless the terms of the trust provide otherwise.

736.0804 Duty to administer trust in good faith.—A trustee shall administer the trust as a prudent person would, by considering the purposes, terms, distributional requirements, and other circumstances of the trust.
736.0805 Information and reports to beneficiaries.—(1) A trustee shall keep the beneficiaries of the trust reasonably informed of the trust and its administration.
736.0812 Duty to avoid conflict of interest.—A trustee shall not cause the trustee to engage in a transaction that the trustee knows or should know involves a conflict of interest with a beneficiary.

222.01 Exemption from forced sale; homestead; how claimed.—(1) The homestead of a natural person is exempt from forced sale under process or judgment of any court or for the payment of taxes or assessments against the homestead or against the person or estate of such owner, whether the homestead is owned in fee simple or in any other estate or interest therein, and whether or not it is used as a family home. The exemption shall be claimed by a record in the public records of the county in which the property is located.

732.401 Exemption of homestead; how claimed; disposition on death; exception.—(1) The homestead of a decedent is exempt from the payment of all debts and claims except those that have preferences against the homestead by virtue of a mortgage, deed of trust, or other contract executed or entered into by the person having an ownership interest in, or title to, the homestead, or his or her spouse, or for obligations in connection with improvements made to the homestead, or for taxes and assessments imposed thereon or obligations relating thereto.

Article X. Miscellaneous Provisions - Section 4. HOMESTEAD. (a) Exemption from forced sale. Any person of the family of a Florida resident has the right, during the lifetime of such person, to claim the benefit of the constitutional exemption of a homestead from forced sale under process or judgment of any court or for the payment of taxes or assessments against the homestead or against the person or estate of such owner.
